title: AutoFill and Flash Fill
summary: Series of numbers, dates and months; filling patterns; splitting names with Flash Fill.
objectives: Use the fill handle to copy values and continue series.
Set the step of a series with two starting cells.
Use Flash Fill (Ctrl+E) to split or join text by example.

p: Start a pattern, drag the **fill handle** at the corner of the selection, and Excel continues it.
Jan → Feb, Mar… Monday → Tuesday… Week 1 → Week 2.
A single number like 5 is just copied.
In real life: Fills a year of month names and membership dates in seconds instead of typing every one.

terms: the small square at the selection's corner

marks.text: drag the small square at the bottom-right corner

p: Select **two** cells first. The gap between them becomes the step.
1, 2 → 3, 4, 5. Then 5, 10 → 15, 20, 25. Then Jan, Mar → May, Jul.
**Double-click** the fill handle to fill down to the end of your data.
In real life: Numbers 1,200 admission forms: types 1 and 2, selects both, and double-clicks the fill handle.

check.q: You select two cells holding 5 and 10, then drag the fill handle down. What comes next?
check.explain: The step is 5, so Excel continues **15**, 20, 25.

why.3: That would repeat the first cell.

p: Type one example of what you want, press **Ctrl+E**, and Excel copies the pattern down the column.
Split names, pull PIN codes out of addresses, join first + last names.
Also on the ribbon: Data › Flash Fill.
In real life: Splits 500 candidate names into first and last names for a mail merge, with one Ctrl+E.

p: Flash Fill guesses from your example, so look through the results.
Fix one wrong row and Excel learns from your correction.
The results are plain values: they won't update if the names change.
In real life: Spotted that every three-word name was split wrongly, fixed one, and Flash Fill corrected the rest.

check.q: You used Flash Fill to split names. Later a full name changes. What happens to its first name?
options: It stays the same, because Flash Fill pastes values
check.explain: Flash Fill results are **values**, not formulas, so they don't update.

demo.intro: Watch AutoFill continue months, numbers, labels and dates.

steps.say: Drag the fill handle from **Jan** across: the months follow.
Select 1 and 2, then drag down: the numbers count on by one.
A date moves on one day at a time.

demo.outro: One or two starting cells, one drag.

lab.intro: Use the fill handle (the small square at the bottom-right of a selection) to build each series. Drag it; don’t type every value.

hints: Drag the fill handle right to M1.
Select both, so Excel sees the step.
Drag the fill handle down to A12.

mistakes.msg: You copied the 1s and 2s. Select both A3 and A4 before dragging, so Excel continues the count.

tasks.prompt: Fill **C3:C9** with one date per day, from **01-11-2026** to **07-11-2026**.

hints: Select both to set the step.

real.title: Split names with Flash Fill
steps: Column A has ten full names. In **B2**, type the first name of A2: *Asha*.
Press **Ctrl+E** (or Data › Flash Fill). Check every result.
In **C2**, type the last name *Rao* and press Ctrl+E again.
